newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Bus signs joint venture in China.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Bus signs joint venture in China.

text.p: Swedish vehicle group Volvo AB on Thursday said its bus division had signed a joint venture agreement in China with the Shanghai Automotive Co Ltd.
Volvo Bus said the 50/50 joint venture will primarily produce and market modern city buses and commuters.
Production will start at the end of 1997 with an initial volumes of 500 units a year.
"This production level is to be regarded as a first step heading for a future, increased market volume," Volvo Bus said in a statement.
It said the Shanghai Municipal Construction Commission will be an important customer for the joint venture.

At a ceremony before Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson in Shanghai, the new joint venture group signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Shanghai Municipal Construction Commission that covers the sale of almost 1,000 buses for use in Shanghai.
Shanghai Automotive Co Ltd (SAC) is 75 percent owned by the state owned Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp and 25 percent by the Shanghai International Trust and Investment Co.
Volvo said in its statement that SAC was set up in 1995 and already has a number of foreign joint ventures in the automotive area.
